label: token right after an early digit 0 in the original sequence
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase on the step right after the digit 0 is input, only early in the sequence (t = 1..5; almost nothing at t >= 6, and never in the copy phase). 94% of activation mass lands on steps where prev_tok = 0 (25x lift). It is strongest when the 0 comes at position 2-3, especially after a sequence starting with v/k/3 (e.g. v k 0 [0] [2]); the step after a 0 0 pair is the top activation. It does not fire on the 0 itself, and it is weak or silent after a second, non-adjacent 0 (z 0 i 0 [y] stays silent). The missed activations are about 30% of active steps but only 6% of mass: weak, diffuse firing at other original-phase steps and the delimiter. On dev: precision 0.90, recall 0.69, F1 0.78, mass recall 0.94.

issues: The predicate's recall is low (0.687, test F1 0.778), but the steps it misses carry little activation. The 30,780 missed active steps hold 6.2% of the mass, and the examples are all tiny (0.00-0.09 of max). They are spread across original-phase steps with no clear pattern: every original-phase step at t=1..5 whose previous token is not 0 has precision 0.013 and holds 5.5% of the mass. The largest single class, prev_tok=y (t<=5), has precision 0.07 and holds 1.2% of the mass. The delimiter step holds 0.6% of the mass at a 0.25% firing rate. None of these is a systematic class worth adding to the predicate.

The t<=5 cutoff is fuzzy. After a 0, the feature fires reliably at t=1 (precision 1.0) and t=3 (0.99), but only about half the time at t=5 (precision 0.43, 2.5% of mass). Most of the predicate's false positives come from t=4-5. Cutting to t<=4 raises precision to 0.979 but lowers F1 to 0.772, so neither cutoff is clearly better.

The other claims check out. The feature never fires in the copy phase (0 active steps). It is almost silent at t>=6 (522 active steps at t=6, 5 at t=7). Firing after a non-adjacent second 0 is weaker (precision 0.57 when two or more 0s were seen before). After a 0 0 pair precision is 0.80. When the sequence starts with v, k or 3, the steps after a 0 at t=3-4 carry about 1.7x more mass per step (precision 1.0). Mass recall on the test split is 0.938.
